messages:
Leo: quick thought — instead of discrete FP8->INT8->4bit hops, what about a "fidelity dimmer" on profiles? a continuous knob to smooth quality/cost tradeoffs.
Anya: curious how that differs from profile priority lists. runtime semantics?
Leo: instead of hard fallback, a profile exposes a dimmer in [0,1]. runtime uses it to interpolate between a higher-fidelity kernel and a low-bit fast kernel (weights/activations blended).
Rachel: neat. main concern is how we define and measure acceptable quality as the dimmer moves. need a small, auditable contract.
Leo: agreed. sketch contract fields: dimmer, min_quality, hysteresis_s, telemetry_tag. runtime will back off dimmer if deg_score > threshold.
Matt: blending kernels will cost extra ops while interpolating. do we have numbers vs doing a single hop fallback?
Leo: prototype numbers: ~5-8% extra matmul work during transitions for affected layers. but avoids abrupt quality cliffs — better UX for chat endpoints.
Anya: ops/rollout requirements: customer opt-out, per-endpoint budget cap, and a safety floor for min_quality. plus hysteresis to avoid flapping.
Rachel: propose example JSON for profile contract: ```{ "profile_name": "dimmer-canary-v1", "dimmer": "0.75", "min_quality": "0.88", "hysteresis_s": "30", "telemetry_tag": "dimmer-canary/2026-03" }```
ci-cd-bot: canary push scheduled (id: cp-9921) :white_check_mark:
Matt: runtime details — adjust dimmer only at token boundaries and only after N stable tokens to avoid jitter. interpolation weight w = dimmer, final kernel = w*high_fid + (1-w)*lowbit.
Anya: agree token-granularity is safer than per-request. also need a daily budget for extra compute to bound cost.
Rachel: telemetry plan — synthetic prompts run every 10m against golden refs. emit a "dimmer_regression" signal and hook to optimize alerts.
Leo: rollout plan: 1) staging canary, 2) 5% prod on low-risk endpoints, 3) monitor deg_score, latency, cost delta. auto-rollback if quality drops >2% or latency >10%.
Matt: I'll build a kernel interpolation prototype + microbenchmarks. will post perf numbers and a short readme.
Anya: I'll draft an RFC follow-up linking contract fields, runtime changes, and rollout checklist. will own playbook.
Rachel: tagging SRE for canary alert thresholds and pagin rules. :triangular_flag_on_post:
SRE: noted — we'll propose thresholds for dimmer_regression and cost delta alerts.
Leo: quick local commands to try: ```# create profile
redwoodctl profiles create --file ./dimmer-canary.json
# rollout 5%
redwoodctl rollout start --endpoint chatbot-prod --profile dimmer-canary-v1 --percent 5```
Anya: one more ops item: include an opt-out customer flag and a runtime flag to disable interpolation for latency-sensitive endpoints.
Leo: summary: add dimmer to profile contract + min_quality + hysteresis, token-granularity interpolation with stable-window, telemetry + synthetic probes, staged canary + auto-rollback. next steps: RFC follow-up (Anya) + kernel prototype (Matt).
